subject: physics
question_text: When is the average speed of a body equal to the magnitude of its average velocity?

verification.note: PREDICTED CELL — not asked by either source book. Unit 3 has no Long Answer section in the Fastrack (pp.6-8) or the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.4-5), so predicted cards are authored as VSAQ or SAQ only. Both the question and the mark split are CLAIMS until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Motion in a Straight Line · 2 marks

steps.label: The condition
lines: They are equal when the body moves along a
straight line in ONE direction only, without
reversing. Then the distance travelled equals
steps.why: The two averages differ only because distance can exceed displacement, and that can happen only if the body doubles back.
common_mistakes: Saying they are equal whenever the path is straight. A body that goes out and comes back moves in a straight line and still differs.

recall.must_convey: That they are equal when the body moves in a straight line in one direction without reversing.

steps.memory_tip: Straight line is not enough — it must also never turn back.
steps.margin_note: The words "without reversing" carry this mark.

steps.label: A counter-example

lines.text: A round trip: displacement 0, distance not 0

lines: A man who walks 2.5 km to a market and back
has average velocity zero but average speed
steps.why: The round trip is the extreme case: the displacement collapses to zero while the distance is the full journey, so the two averages could not differ more.
common_mistakes: Giving an example that does not reverse, which cannot show any difference.

recall.must_convey: That for a round trip the average velocity is zero while the average speed is not.

steps.memory_tip: Round trip: velocity averages to zero, speed does not. Best possible counter-example.
steps.margin_note: Name both averages in the example.

insider_note: One condition, one counter-example. The counter-example is what shows the condition is needed.
